rows.grounds: compound: śuddha+sphaṭika+sannibha; likeness to pure crystal

items.question: What luminous abode should be reached as the object of meditation?
premises: The eternal-shiva-abode is attained.
That abode resembles pure crystal.
items.inference: Meditation is directed toward the pure crystal-like abode of Sadāśiva.
items.plain_english: Having reached the abode of Sadāśiva, which resembles pure crystal.

items.question: How continually should the mind visualize the bliss-filled abode?
premises: The abode is filled with hosts of great bliss.
Visualization is performed with the mind.
The practice is to be constant.
items.inference: One should always mentally visualize the abode filled with hosts of great bliss.
items.plain_english: One should always visualize with the mind that abode filled with hosts of great bliss.

items.question: What ecstatic transformation arises in the living being through this visualization?
premises: Bliss causes the hair to stand on end.
The living being undergoes a change in that state.
items.inference: In that blissful thrill, the living being becomes transformed, O beautiful one.
items.plain_english: O beautiful one, in that state where bliss makes the hair stand on end, the living being becomes transformed.

items.question: What captivating physical attributes characterize the visualized divine form?
premises: The form is filled with many gems.
The form is long-armed.
The form captivates the mind.
items.inference: The divine form to be visualized is gem-filled, long-armed, and captivating.
items.plain_english: Visualize him as filled with many gems, long-armed, and captivating to the mind.

items.question: What ornaments adorn the ears and body of the visualized form?
premises: The ears are endowed with earrings.
The form is adorned with a gem necklace.
items.inference: The visualized form is adorned with earrings and a gem necklace.
items.plain_english: His ears are adorned with earrings, and he is beautified by a necklace of gems.

items.question: Which iconic features identify Śiva in this gross visualization?
premises: The form has eight arms.
The form has three eyes.
The form has lotus-petal eyes.
items.inference: The visualized deity is Śiva with eight arms, three eyes, and lotus-petal eyes.
items.plain_english: Visualize Śiva as eight-armed, three-eyed, and with eyes like lotus petals.

items.question: What gross bodily form of Śiva should be visualized in this manner?
premises: The preceding verses describe specific attributes.
The instruction concerns Śiva's gross body.
items.inference: One should thus visualize the gross body of Śiva, O lotus-faced one.
items.plain_english: O lotus-faced one, one should thus visualize his gross body.

rows.grounds: sūkṣmam + tu; contrasts with gross form

items.question: How is the subtle divine form distinguished from the gross body?
premises: The subtle form is supreme and divine.
The subtle form is without effort.
The subtle form is always like inert stillness.
items.inference: The subtle form is supreme, divine, actionless, and always still like the inert.
uncertainties: jaḍavat may indicate transcendent stillness rather than literal insentience
items.plain_english: But the subtle form is supreme, divine, without effort, and always like something inert.

rows.grounds: compound: sthūla+dhyāna; meditation on gross form

items.question: What spiritual attainment results from performing meditation on the gross form?
premises: Gross meditation is performed.
Liberation is presented as attainable.
items.inference: By performing gross meditation, one may obtain liberation, O great goddess.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, having performed meditation on the gross form, one may obtain liberation.

items.question: What initial ritual act must precede further practice with the gross body?
premises: Practice begins at first.
The gross body is the object of worship.
items.inference: At first one should worship the gross body, O goddess, O lotus-faced one.
items.plain_english: O goddess, O lotus-faced one, first having worshipped the gross body.

rows.grounds: tejas + ca; element or principle named
prakṛtiḥ + mohinī + iti fused in text; identifies deluding nature

items.question: How is the deluding nature identified in relation to radiance and prakṛti?
premises: Radiance is mentioned.
Prakṛti is called deluding.
items.inference: Radiance and the deluding prakṛti are identified as such, O supreme goddess.
uncertainties: Token sequence is irregular and may reflect textual corruption or repetition
items.plain_english: And radiance, O supreme goddess, and prakṛti is called deluding, thus.

items.question: Why is śakti declared to hold primacy in all forms of worship?
premises: A reason has been indicated by therefore.
The scope includes all worships.
Śakti is named as foremost.
items.inference: Therefore śakti is said to have primacy in all worships.
items.plain_english: Therefore, in all worships, śakti is said to have primacy.

items.question: How should meditation on the subtle body relate to placing the gross form?
premises: Meditation on the subtle body is performed.
The gross form is placed there.
items.inference: After meditating on the subtle body, one should indeed place the gross form there.
items.plain_english: Having performed meditation on the subtle body, one should indeed place the gross form there.

items.question: What distinctive colors and adornments mark the visualized divine form?
premises: The form is dark-hued.
The form wears yellow garments.
The form is adorned with a forest garland.
items.inference: The visualized form is dark, yellow-garmented, and adorned with a forest garland.
items.plain_english: Visualize him as dark-hued, wearing yellow garments, and adorned with a forest garland.

items.question: What sacred marks and ornaments distinguish the chest of the visualized form?
premises: The chest bears the śrīvatsa mark.
The chest is adorned with a gem necklace.
items.inference: The chest is distinguished by the śrīvatsa mark and a gem necklace.
items.plain_english: His chest is adorned with the śrīvatsa mark and beautified by a necklace of gems.

items.question: What serene facial feature and foot ornament complete the visualized form?
premises: The eyes are serene like lotuses.
Anklets are at the feet.
items.inference: The form has serene lotus-like eyes and anklets at the feet, O beloved one.
uncertainties: nūpuraṃ is singular in form though caraṇe is dual; may imply anklets collectively
items.plain_english: O beloved one, visualize him with serene lotus-like eyes and anklets at his feet.

items.question: How pervasively does the visualized form fill the world in meditation?
premises: The form fills the world.
This filling is constant.
items.inference: The visualized form constantly fills the world, O goddess, O lotus-faced one.
items.plain_english: O goddess, O lotus-faced one, visualize him as constantly filling the world.

rows.grounds: compound: prakṛti+rūpin; formed of subtle prakṛti

items.question: What is the essential nature of the subtle body in this teaching?
premises: The subtle body is motionless.
It is formed of subtle prakṛti.
items.inference: The subtle, motionless body is indeed of the nature of subtle prakṛti.
items.plain_english: Indeed the subtle, motionless body is of the form of subtle prakṛti.

items.question: Which three contemplative practices are introduced for definition in this context?
premises: Meditation is named.
Concentration is named.
Absorption is named.
items.inference: Meditation, concentration, and absorption are the three practices introduced, O pure-smiled one.
items.plain_english: O pure-smiled one, as for meditation, concentration, and absorption.

items.question: How is meditation defined in terms of contemplating the divine form?
premises: Meditation is the subject of definition.
It involves contemplation of all limbs.
items.inference: Meditation is the contemplation of all limbs, O supreme goddess, O beloved one.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, O beloved one, meditation is the contemplation of all the limbs.

items.question: What attentive instruction is given regarding the definition of concentration?
premises: A definition called dhāraṇā is to be stated.
Pārvatī is asked to listen respectfully.
items.inference: Pārvatī is instructed to listen respectfully to what is called concentration.
items.plain_english: But hear respectfully, O Pārvatī, what is called concentration.

rows.grounds: samādhiḥ + vijñeyaḥ fused in text; identifies samādhi

items.question: Why should absorption be recognized without further discursive inquiry?
premises: This state is to be known as absorption.
Inquiry is not to be done here.
items.inference: This should be known as absorption, and no further inquiry should be made here.
uncertainties: vijñeyo appears twice, possibly emphatic repetition or textual irregularity
items.plain_english: This should be known as absorption; no further inquiry should be made here.

items.question: What fundamental nature is attributed to all that has been taught?
premises: The teaching is spoken by the speaker.
All of it is characterized as consisting of śakti.
items.inference: All that has been spoken is declared to consist of śakti, O goddess.
items.plain_english: O goddess, all that I have spoken is remembered as consisting of śakti.

items.question: How should worship, meditation, and recitation be integrated in practice?
premises: Worship is performed.
Meditation is performed.
Recitation is to be carried out.
items.inference: Having performed worship and meditation accordingly, one should perform recitation.
items.plain_english: Having performed worship and meditation accordingly, one should perform recitation.
